title: Crowd Artists
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Crowd Artist based in Canada.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Crowd Artist to help bring large-scale film and television environments to life.
You will create dynamic, believable crowds that add scale, energy, and realism to complex scenes.
Working within a small and highly collaborative production team, you will combine artistic judgment with technical simulation expertise.
The role involves setting up crowd assets, creating simulations, troubleshooting workflows, and delivering production-ready results.
You will collaborate closely with FX, Look Development, Lighting, Animation, and CG leadership to ensure seamless integration.
The position offers the chance to contribute to a major Marvel Studios streaming production while working in a supportive, creative environment.
This is a fully remote opportunity across Canada, with the option to work from a Vancouver studio.

Accountabilities:

  • Crowd simulation: Populate environments with characters and assets using crowd simulation techniques to create vibrant, believable scenes at scale.
  • Asset setup: Prepare and configure digital crowd assets and develop Atoms simulations for more complex character behaviors and shot requirements.
  • Troubleshooting: Identify and resolve simulation, setup, and workflow issues while testing new approaches to maintain production efficiency and quality.
  • Creative integration: Work closely with FX, Look Development, Lighting, Animation, and CG Supervisors to ensure crowd elements align with the visual direction of each sequence.
  • Cross-functional collaboration: Communicate proactively with other departments regarding creative solutions, workflow improvements, technical requirements, and production handoffs.
  • Production delivery: Manage assigned tasks and deadlines effectively, provide regular progress updates, and consistently deliver high-quality work within production schedules.
  • Workflow improvement: Contribute ideas and practical solutions that improve crowd creation, simulation, and integration workflows across the production.

    • Requirements:

    • Professional experience: 2+ years of experience working on feature films, episodic television, or animated features, with a strong focus on crowd work.
    • Crowd simulation expertise: Hands-on experience creating digital crowd assets and running complex simulations using Atoms.
    • Artistic and technical ability: Strong understanding of crowd movement and behavior, combined with a strong artistic eye and the ability to balance visual quality with technical requirements.
    • Problem-solving: Ability to investigate technical challenges, experiment with workflows, and develop practical solutions independently.
    • Collaboration: Strong communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to work effectively across multiple CG and production departments.
    • Production awareness: Strong time-management skills and the ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and communicate proactively about progress or challenges.
    • Work authorization: Must be legally eligible to work in Canada.
    • Linux: Familiarity with Linux-based operating systems is an asset.
    • Crowd workflows: Experience with background crowd simulation methods and production workflows is an asset.
    • Production tracking: Working knowledge of Flow Production Tracking, formerly ShotGrid, is an asset.
    • Additional software: Experience with other crowd tools such as Houdini or Golaem is considered an advantage.
    • Portfolio: A professional portfolio or demo reel demonstrating relevant crowd and simulation work is expected.
    • Availability: Ability to start within the required production window of late October to mid-November 2026.

      • Benefits:

      • Competitive compensation: CAD $83,000–$92,000 annually, depending on experience and level.
      • Remote flexibility: Fully remote position available anywhere in Canada.
      • Vancouver option: Access to a Vancouver studio for those who prefer working in person.
      • Major production exposure: Opportunity to contribute to a large-scale Marvel Studios streaming series.
      • Healthcare coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits.
      • Collaborative culture: Supportive and connected working environment that values creativity, communication, and teamwork.
      • Inclusive workplace: Commitment to diversity, inclusion, accessibility, and creating an environment where employees can thrive.
      • Location priority: Priority may be given to candidates residing in British Columbia, as well as Canadian citizens and permanent residents.

title: Solutions Architect, Retail/E-commerce, Solutions Architecture
description:
Are you passionate about helping retail and e-commerce customers solve complex business and technical challenges using cloud technologies? Do you enjoy architecting AI-powered solutions that transform customer experiences, optimize supply chains, and drive digital commerce innovation? Do you thrive on being a trusted technical advisor who partners with customers from strategy through production?

AWS Sales, Marketing, and Global Services (SMGS) is responsible for driving revenue, adoption, and growth from the largest and fastest growing small- and mid-market accounts to enterprise-level customers including public sector. We work with leading retail, e-commerce, and consumer packaged goods (CPG) companies that are building mission-critical, customer-facing applications on AWS — and we believe that exceptional technical guidance is critical to their success.

As a Solutions Architect within Amazon Web Services (AWS), you will have the opportunity to help shape and execute a strategy to build deep engagement and broad adoption of AWS services across retail and e-commerce customers. You will focus on key industry themes including **Generative AI and Agentic AI** (Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Kiro), **unified commerce**, **real-time personalization**, **retail media networks (RMN)**, **supply chain optimization**, **data and analytics modernization**, and **application modernization** — helping customers leverage the full breadth of the AWS platform to accelerate their business transformation.

You will own the technical engagement and ultimate success of specific customer initiatives — from discovery and architecture design through proof-of-concept, implementation, and production launch. You will develop deep expertise in AWS technologies while building broad industry knowledge of how modern retail and e-commerce solutions are architected on AWS, including Well-Architected best practices, migration, and modernization patterns.

A successful candidate will possess strong customer-facing skills to represent AWS effectively with senior business and technical stakeholders, combined with a technical depth that enables meaningful collaboration with software developers, data engineers, and architects. Experience with AI/ML or generative AI use cases, familiarity with retail industry trends — including **brick-and-mortar retail operations, omnichannel distribution, and retail media** — and the ability to architect end-to-end solutions spanning data, AI, and modern application architectures are highly valued.

Key job responsibilities
- Act as a trusted technical advisor to retail and e-commerce customers, designing cloud architectures that address industry-specific challenges including unified commerce, retail media networks, supply chain optimization, and AI-powered personalization.

- Lead technical discovery and solution design workshops with customer stakeholders (from developers to C-suite), defining clear objectives, success criteria, and architectural roadmaps.

- Drive hands-on proof-of-concept builds and architecture reviews, leveraging AWS services across Generative AI (Bedrock, Kiro), data & analytics, and application modernization to accelerate customer outcomes.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Account Managers, Specialist SAs, ProServe, and AWS Partners to deliver end-to-end solutions and ensure successful production launches.

- Develop and share reusable assets, reference architectures, and
industry best practices with the broader SA community and retail
customer base — contributing to thought leadership through blogs,
workshops, and customer events.

- Stay current on retail industry trends and emerging AWS capabilities,
translating them into actionable recommendations for customers.

A day in the life
No two days are the same. You might lead a whiteboard architecture session with a retailer building their retail media network, run a Well-Architected review ahead of a peak sales event, or build a generative AI proof-of-concept for personalized recommendations. Other days, you'll join executive briefings with C-level stakeholders, collaborate with Account Managers and Specialist SAs on competitive deals, or deep-dive into a customer's supply chain architecture. You will work closely with Taiwan's most innovative retail, e-commerce, and CPG brands — helping them stay ahead in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

title: Ylilääkäri, Tyks Yleislääketieteen palvelualue, Turku
description:
Ylilääkärin virkaan voidaan liittää palvelualuejohtajan lisätehtävä ja virkaan haetaan henkilöä, joka voi toimia palvelualuejohtajan roolissa.

Yleislääketieteen palvelualueeseen kuuluu neljä vastuualuetta: Yleislääketieteen (itäinen ja läntinen) vastuualue, geriatrian vastuualue sekä palliatiivinen keskus ja kotisairaala. Yleislääketieteen palvelualue kuuluu tulosryhmään 1 yhdessä Medisiinisen palvelualueen ja Päivystyksen palvelualueen kanssa.

Tehtäväsi

Ylilääkärinä johdat terveyden- ja sairaanhoitoa ja vastaat palvelualueesi talousarvion valmistelusta ja noudattamisesta. Lisäksi vastaat palvelualueen terveyspalvelujen tuottamisesta asukkaille, palvelutuotannon mitoittamisesta vastaamaan palvelutarpeita sekä palvelualueen saumattomasta yhteistyöstä muiden toimijoiden kanssa. Vastaat osaltasi myös palvelualueen opetuksen ja tutkimuksen edellytysten toteutumisesta.

Ylilääkäri vastaa palvelualueensa taloudesta, resurssien jaosta ja prosessien toimivuudesta ja sujuvuudesta yhteistoiminnassa vastuualuejohtajien ja ylihoitajien kanssa. Keskeiset yhteistyökumppanit ovat palvelualueen vastuualuejohtajat, ylihoitajat, tulosryhmäjohtaja, muut tulosryhmän palvelualuejohtajat sekä yliopistolliset toimijat. Halutessaan ylilääkäri voi käyttää työajastaan enintään 20 % kliiniseen potilastyöhön.

Mitä tarjoamme sinulle

Tarjoamme sinulle keskeisen ja vaikuttavan johtamistehtävän sekä mahdollisuuden osallistua palvelualuetta uudistavaan ja kehittävään työhön. Pääset johtamaan laajaa ja monipuolista kokonaisuutta, jossa strateginen ja tietoon perustuva päätöksenteko on keskeistä.

Palkkaus on lääkärisopimuksen mukainen uraporraspalkkaus. Lisäksi voidaan maksaa työkokemuslisää ja mahdollista henkilökohtaista lisää. Palvelualuejohtajan tehtävään liittyy tehtävälisä.

Mitä odotamme sinulta

Odotamme sinulta kykyä johtaa tuloksellisesti tietoon perustuen, muutosvalmiutta ja aktiivista uusien kokonaisuuksien eteenpäin viemistä vahvasti säännellyssä toimintaympäristössä sekä kykyä luoda visioita ja innostaa henkilöstöä. Arvostamme myös valmiuksia asiakaskokemuksen kehittämiseen, hyviä vuorovaikutus- ja verkostoitumistaitoja, kykyä vahvistaa yhteistyötä eri toimijoiden välillä sekä kykyä toimia luottamuksen rakentajana ja ylläpitäjänä.

Lisäksi eduksi luetaan:

- kokemus ja näyttö menestyksekkäästä/tuloksellisesta tietoon perustuvasta toiminnan, talouden, henkilöstön ja prosessien johtamisesta
- vahva kokemus julkisesta hallinnosta
- hyvät näyttöön perustuvat henkilöstöjohtamisen taidot
- vahva kokemus strategisesta johtamisesta sekä muutosjohtamisesta ja kehittämisestä
- kokemus verkostojohtamisesta ja toimimisesta oman alan verkostoissa
- hyvät esiintymis- ja viestintätaidot

Kelpoisuusvaatimuksena on terveydenhuollon ammattihenkilöistä annetussa laissa 559/94 säädetty laillistus tai lupa toimia lääkärin tehtävissä, erikoislääkärin pätevyys virkaan soveltuvalla erikoisalalla ja kokemusta erikoislääkärin pätevyyttä edellyttävistä tehtävistä sekä kokemusta alan johtamisesta ja kehittämisestä tai soveltuvaa johtamiskoulutusta. Dosentuuri sekä tohtorin tutkinto katsotaan eduksi.

Viran kielitaitovaatimuksena on hyvä suullinen ja kirjallinen suomen kielen taito ja tyydyttävä suullinen ja kirjallinen ruotsin kielen taito.

Hae tehtävään ja tule johtamaan, kehittämään ja rakentamaan tulevaisuuden yleislääketieteen palveluita.

Virkaan valittavalle voidaan teettää turvallisuusselvityslain mukainen turvallisuusselvitys, joka hyväksyttynä on edellytys virkamääräykselle.

title: Program Manager - Procurement Process Improvement & Excellence, Data Center Procurement Governance (DCPG)
description:
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

The Data Center Procurement Governance (DCPG) function is part of AIS. Do you want to be part of a global team that relentlessly pursues procurement excellence, improves operational processes and outcomes, and manages compliance and business risks? Do you have a solid procurement background, excel at program and stakeholder management, and thrive in a fast-paced environment?

We are hiring a Program Manager - Procurement Excellence to work closely with procurement stakeholders, operations, functions, systems and engineering to enable scalable, well-controlled business processes and decision-making.

This role sits within a broader team of program managers that operates as highly embedded business partners to procurement, focused on operational effectiveness and impact, scalable mechanisms, and risk-informed execution.

The ideal candidate combines strong business process thinking, stakeholder influence, operational rigor, and technical literacy to help teams move quickly while maintaining appropriate risk and control standards.

The ideal candidate require a high tolerance of ambiguity aligned to AWS Day 1 culture, ability to influence executive decisions, drive strategic initiatives and change management that deliver meaningful programmatic improvements.

This is not a traditional audit or policy-focused role. We designed this role for individuals who enjoy solving operational problems, driving influence and alignment across teams, and building scalable mechanisms in fast-paced environments. Over time, this role has opportunity to evolve toward broader technical program management style leadership responsibilities.

Your role:

Business Partnership & Operational Enablement
• Partner closely with Technical, Engineering, Operations, Procurement, and Risk stakeholders to shape scalable business processes and controls.
• Engage early with teams to influence decisions, identify risks, and enable efficient execution.
• Translate risk and controls requirements into practical, actionable operating mechanisms.

Risk & Controls Integration
• Design and improve scalable controls, guardrails, and operational frameworks that support business velocity while managing risk appropriately.
• Simplify and modernize existing processes to align with evolving business needs and risk appetite.
• Ensure controls are operationally practical and embedded into day-to-day workflows.

Business Process & Mechanism Ownership
• Identify process gaps, friction points, and operational inefficiencies across programs and workflows.
• Build mechanisms, playbooks, decision frameworks, and scalable patterns that improve consistency and reduce ambiguity.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives across governance, operational readiness, and execution processes.

Cross-Functional Coordination & Audit Readiness
• Act as a business partner to Procurement teams and a key coordination point across Risk, Audit, Assurance, Legal, Technical and Engineering teams.
• Streamline audit readiness and evidence gathering through scalable operational processes rather than manual coordination.
• Ensure teams have clarity on ownership, expectations, and escalation paths.

Technical & Operational Collaboration
• Engage effectively with technical teams by understanding system architecture, workflows, dependencies, and operational trade-offs.
• Partner with engineering teams to ensure controls and operational requirements are designed into solutions early.
• Use data and operational signals to identify risks, trends, and improvement opportunities.

What good looks like for this role:
• Procurement teams and functional partners proactively engage you as a trusted partner early in planning and execution.
• Decisions move faster because of your involvement, not slower.
• Processes become simpler, clearer, and more scalable over time.
• Risk Management and controls are embedded into operational workflows rather than managed as separate activities.
• Stakeholders experience clear ownership, practical guidance, and streamlined engagement across governance functions.

What We Are Not Looking For
• Purely policy or checklist-driven approaches.
• Candidates who operate primarily through approvals or gatekeeping or arm's length approach
• Candidates who identify problems without driving practical solutions.

High stakeholder engagement, influencing and cross-functional ownership is essential is for the role.

Key job responsibilities
• Lead various audit programs, risk remediation, policy and process improvement projects internally and with external stakeholders
• Take lead in establishing necessary controls, mechanisms, and policies to improve DCSP compliance and assurance
• Drive culture of innovation, simplification and continuous improvement through best practice sharing, advocacy and hands-on leadership and execution of projects
• Identify new tools and business processes that simplify, standardize and enable operational excellence
• Derive actionable insights and routinely present recommendations from analysis

A day in the life
-This role has a global scope so there is no standard day - there is much variety in the day
-You could be starting with a morning meeting speaking with US team members, a coffee with APAC and finish up with a call with EMEA
-You will work on multiple projects with global teams, stakeholders and customers
-Your biggest customers will be our Data Center Services Procurement teams and our AWS security assurance teams. Stakeholders also include legal, finance, H&S and other Data Center Communities colleagues

Data Center Procurement Governance (DCPG) is a global function that includes:

-Program Management - a team of Program Managers who are strong business partners to procurement, intersect business process with technology and tooling across the procurement life cycle, to identify, architect and deliver impact projects for our DC procurement teams.

Procurement Systems, Tools & Analytics - Define, support and drive procurement technical roadmap in systems, tooling, automation, analytics and GenAI.

title: Archivist
description:
Te Whiwhinga mahi | The opportunity

We are looking for a passionate and experienced archivist to join our team on a fixed-term basis.

This is a fantastic opportunity to work with unique archival collections and play an important role in ensuring they are cared for, accessible, and used by students, academics, researchers, and members of the wider community.

In this role, you'll support the management of archival collections across their lifecycle — from acquisition and accessioning through to arrangement, description, access, and use. You'll also contribute to outreach and engagement activities that help bring these collections to life and encourage their use by a diverse range of audiences.

The focus of this role will be on the Archive of Māori and Pacific Sound repository, providing an exciting opportunity to work with culturally significant audio collections and contribute to their ongoing care, management, and accessibility.

You'll respond to access requests, supply archival items, develop collection records using ArchivesSpace, and support the care and maintenance of specialist audio equipment.

You'll also contribute to Reading Room services and wider Cultural Collections projects and initiatives, including outreach activities and collection audits.

This is an ideal role for someone who combines strong archival practice with excellent customer service and a genuine interest in cultural collections, particularly Māori and Pacific collections.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Caring for and managing archival collections through acquisition, accessioning, arrangement, description, access, and use.
  • Supporting the Archive of Māori and Pacific Sound repository, including responding to access requests and supplying collection items.
  • Developing and maintaining collection records using the ArchivesSpace archival management system.
  • Supporting the care and maintenance of analogue audio equipment and associated collection materials.
  • Contributing to Reading Room service delivery and providing a welcoming, high-quality experience for collection users.
  • Supporting Cultural Collections projects, outreach activities, audits, and other initiatives that increase engagement with the collections.

This is a full-time, 37.5-hour-per-week role on a 12-month fixed-term contract. The salary range for this role is $73,400 - $78,600 per annum, depending on experience and qualifications.

For more information, please review the Position Description.

He kōrero mōu | About you

You are an enthusiastic and knowledgeable archivist who enjoys working with collections and helping people discover and engage with them.

You bring strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and a high level of customer service. You're comfortable working independently while also enjoying being part of a collaborative team.

You'll have an interest in cultural collections and, ideally, experience working with diverse communities and cultural materials. An understanding of te reo Māori, te ao Māori, tikanga Māori, or a Pacific language would be highly valued.

The opportunity to work with analogue sound collections will particularly appeal to someone interested in audio technology and in the preservation and management of historic sound recordings.

Ngā pūkenga motuhake | Important skills and experience

  • Experience working with archival or cultural collections and an understanding of archival collection management.
  • Strong customer service skills and confidence working with students, academics, researchers, and members of the public.
  • Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage the collection of information accurately.
  • Experience working with collection management or archival systems; familiarity with ArchivesSpace would be an advantage.
  • Experience working respectfully and effectively with people from diverse cultural backgrounds.

The following would be highly beneficial:

  • Knowledge of te reo Māori, te ao Māori, and tikanga Māori.
  • Knowledge of a Pacific language or Pacific cultures.
  • Experience working with analogue audio technologies such as cassettes and open-reel tapes.
  • Knowledge of audio and AV file formats, software, and systems used to manage or manipulate digital audio.

Ngā āhuatanga kei a mātou | What we offer

The University of Auckland is New Zealand's leading University and maintains significant computational, laboratory, and analytic facilities. Auckland is frequently rated as one of the world's most liveable cities.

The University is committed to providing an excellent working environment through the following:

  • Flexible employment practices (including working from home and flexible hours)
  • Up to 6.75% company superannuation scheme
  • A competitive salary with five weeks' annual leave

In addition, we also offer career development programs, discounted car parking, a generous parental leave allowance, childcare, and other discounts on internal and external services.

For more information, please visit Staff Benefits.

Applications must be submitted online by the closing date of 1/09/2026 to be considered. Please include your cover letter and CV highlighting how you can meet the abovementioned skills and experiences.

Please note that we may close the advert earlier if we find a suitable candidate.

title: Senior Research Assistant
description:

Teleradiology Solutions (TRS) is a pioneer in teleradiology, delivering round-the-clock diagnostic radiology reporting and support to hospitals and healthcare providers across India, the US, and other global markets. Founded in 2002 by two Yale-trained physicians and headquartered in Ardmore, PA, TRS today serves over 150 hospitals across 21 countries.
The company pairs a network of board-certified radiologists — including ABR-certified specialists — with technology-driven workflows and its AI-enabled arm, dAIgnostiX, to deliver fast, accurate, and reliable imaging interpretation. dAIgnostiX is based out of Bengaluru (Whitefield). TRS/dAIX also maintains an active academic focus () and ongoing research interests, including AI in radiology.

Department: Clinical Training & Research

Job Title: Sr Research Assistant

Job description:

Research in the field of medicine with a focus on Radiology/Cardiology, Teleradiology, Emergency Imaging, Deep Learning/Artificial Intelligence.

Writing scientific articles with a goal to publish in journals of repute.

title: Unit Facility Management Specialist, Ingka AB Barkarby
description:
Gillar du ny teknik och vill skapa en säker och härlig shoppingupplevelse för kunder samt en säker arbetsmiljö för kollegor. Är du också handlingskraftig och trivs i kontakten med andra, såväl kollegor som leverantörer? Härligt, då har jag goda nyheter!

Mitt namn är Rickard Pellebergs och jag är Unit Facility Manager på Ingka Real Estate. Jag söker nu en kollega till vårt FM-team i Barkarby, Stockholm, som har kunskap och intresse för tekniskt underhåll och fastighetsdrift. Vi är ett team på tre personer med stora kontaktytor till såväl fastighetsägare, service partners, projekt och hyresgäster.

Vem är du?
I den här rollen är du en ambassadör för IKEA och Facility Management. Du får möjlighet att arbeta med din passion för service och teknik tillsammans med härliga människor i en utvecklande miljö. Det innebär att du säkerställer och tar ansvar för att leverera högkvalitativa, kostnadseffektiva och hållbara tjänster, samt nytänkande fastighetslösningar som uppfyller verksamhetens krav idag och imorgon.
Eftersom du kommer att ha löpande dialog med många olika aktörer, tror vi att du är en duktig relationsbyggare som gärna delar med dig av kunskap och samarbetar med andra. Du kan vara kravställande och tydlig på ett ödmjukt sätt. Du är van vid att arbeta mot deadlines och har förmågan att prioritera och planerar ditt arbete. Men viktigast av allt, du delar våra värderingar och visar det i ditt sätt att kommunicera och bemöta människor!
Det är ett krav att du har erfarenhet och utbildning inom fastighetsbranschen. Har du erfarenhet inom områden som tekniska styrsystem, energioptimering och entreprenörshantering eller motsvarigt är det meriterande. B-körkort är ett krav. Du behöver kunna behärska både svenska och engelska i tal och skrift.

En dag i ditt liv med oss
Tillsammans med dina kollegor kommer du att säkerställa att våra fastigheter kan ta emot kunder och medarbetare på bästa sätt. Vi tänker proaktivt för att möta kraven både internt och från myndigheter. Tillsammans levererar vi konkuranskraftiga, hållbara och innovativa fastighetslösningar.
Rollen har mer administrativa arbetsuppgifter än praktiska då externa tekniker kommer att utföra själva underhållet. Du kommer ha ett ansvarsområde där du arbetsleder och tilldelar planerade arbeten, gör beställningar till leverantörer följer upp leveranser och rapporterar tillbaka till ditt team.
Dina huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifter är:
• Underhålla fastigheten och tillgångarna med ett långsiktigt perspektiv för att möta verksamhetensbehov både idag och i framtiden.
• Samordna och dokumentera operativa uppgifter relaterade till internt arbete, samt tjänster som utförs av externa leverantörer.
• Planera, styra och följa upp fastighetsrelaterade tjänster inom bland annat renhållning och tekniskt underhåll för den fastighet du ansvarar för.
• Följa upp tillstånd, licenser, certifikat och rapporter. Utföra kontroller för att säkerställa att lokal och nationell lagstiftning samt interna regelverk följs.
• Vara ett stöd i upphandlingar gällande fastighetstjänster och ha löpande kontakt med leveranstörer.
• Bidra med kunskaper för budget – och prognosarbetet tillsammans med Facility Manager.
• Delta i projekt som drivs av fastighet eller andra funktioner på varuhuset, såsom större byggprojekt eller lokala ombyggnationer.

Vårt team på IKEA
Ingka AB är ett servicebolag och ett av de första företagen Ingvar Kamprad grundade. Varje dag levererar vi tjänster och kompetens inom HR, Finance, Workplace och Real Estate till andra IKEA bolag. På så sätt kan de fokusera på sin kärnverksamhet. Och tillsammans bidrar vi till att skapa en bättre vardag för de många människorna!
Inom Real Estate i Sverige jobbar ungefär 120 medarbetare med allt från Real Estate Development och Asset Management till Construction och Facility Management. Vi finns från Malmö i söder till Haparanda i norr.

Frågor om tjänsten – Låt oss knyta kontakt!
Tjänsten vi erbjuder är en tillsvidareanställning med provanställning 6 månader.
Tjänsten är på heltid med placering i Barkarby, Stockholm.
Arbetstider är dagtid på vardagar.

Har du frågor om tjänsten är du välkommen att kontakta rekryterande chef:
Rickard Pelleberg, rickard.pellebergs@ingka.ikea.com

Har du frågor om rekryteringsprocessen kontakta rekryterare:
Ellen Lindholm, ellen.lindholm1@ingka.ikea.com

title: ResQ Market Lead
description:
Some careers start with a job. Others start by building a business.

At ResQ Club, we’re on a mission to eliminate food waste. Every day, we help thousands of people rescue perfectly good food while creating value for restaurants, retailers and the planet.

This September, we’re launching our first ResQ Market pick-up location in Ruoholahti—a completely new business area for ResQ. We’re looking for an ambitious ResQ Market Lead to help build and run it from day one.

This isn’t a traditional store manager role but requires hands-on work.

One day you’ll be running the market, that is for example offloading deliveries, filling shelves and fridges, checking temperatures, keeping the store clean and safe, managing inventory, and making sure our in-house control is done properly and creating an outstanding customer experience. The next, you’ll be negotiating with suppliers, meeting HoReCa buyers, analysing sales data, or working with our leadership team to develop how ResQ Market should grow.

If you’re excited by ownership, variety and the opportunity to build something new, this could be the role that accelerates your career.

This role is designed for future business leaders

ResQ Market is a new growth vertical within ResQ Club. You’ll work directly with senior leadership to develop how the concept operates, grows and scales.

You’ll gain first-hand experience across every aspect of building a business:

  • Retail operations

  • Commercial partnerships

  • B2B sales

  • Category and assortment development

  • Pricing and commercial performance

  • Business development and strategy

We’re not looking for someone who already has all the answers. We’re looking for someone who learns quickly, takes ownership and enjoys solving new problems.

If you’re successful in this role, your responsibilities could grow from leading one location to expanding the concept, developing commercial strategy, building new partnerships, leading a team and helping shape one of ResQ’s future growth businesses.

What you’ll do

You’ll take full ownership of the day-to-day business of ResQ Market while helping shape its future.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Running the hands-on daily operations of the ResQ Market and delivering an exceptional customer experience.

  • Receiving, merchandising and managing surplus food and other products.

  • Building and maintaining relationships with food producers, wholesalers and other supply partners.

  • Developing commercial relationships with HoReCa customers and other B2B buyers.

  • Analysing sales, inventory and customer behaviour to improve commercial performance.

  • Testing new operating models, pricing approaches and services.

  • Identifying opportunities to improve the customer experience and operational efficiency.

  • Working closely with the leadership team to define how ResQ Market evolves into a scalable business.

As ResQ Market grows, you’ll have the opportunity to grow with it—from operating the business to helping lead and scale it.

Who we’re looking for

This role is ideal for an ambitious early-career professional who wants to learn faster than they would in a traditional graduate programme.

You likely have:

  • A university degree (or are close to graduating) in business, economics, industrial engineering, entrepreneurship or a related field.

  • Around 1–5 years of relevant experience through work, internships, student organisations or entrepreneurial projects.

  • Strong analytical and commercial thinking.

  • Excellent communication skills and confidence working with customers and partners.

  • An entrepreneurial mindset and comfort working in a fast-changing environment.

  • A willingness to roll up your sleeves—whether that’s serving customers, organising deliveries or negotiating commercial agreements.

  • Fluency in Finnish and English.

Experience in retail, food, marketplaces, startups or B2B sales is an advantage, but not a requirement. Curiosity, ownership and the ability to learn quickly matter more.

Good to know

  • Since pick-ups happen mostly in the evenings, your typical working hours are 11–19 or 12–20

  • You'll report directly to leadership on how the business side develops, not just on day-to-day store operations

  • As ResQ Market grows, so can your role. This could mean expanding to more locations, leading a team, or helping shape one of ResQ's next growth businesses

  • We welcome you to start as soon as possible

  • The monthly salary range for this position is 4 000 - 4 700 euros depending on your previous experience and knowledge

Why join ResQ?

At ResQ, you’ll have an opportunity that’s difficult to find elsewhere.

You’ll think like a founder, learn like a consultant and execute like an operator.

description:

title: Intake Case Worker
description:
Number of Positions Available:

1

ABOUT US

The Salvation Army is a Christian movement and one of Australia's largest and most-loved charities. We believe in doing good that transforms lives and futures for the better. It is this belief which drives us to find new ways and places where we can make a difference. From times of personal crisis to moments of national grief, we are always here — providing support, safety, community, and opportunity.

About the Role

As a key member of The Salvation Army’s ACT Central Intake Service (CIS) team, the Intake Case Worker plays a vital role in delivering high-quality, trauma-informed intake, assessment, and short-term case coordination to individuals and families experiencing hardship, housing instability, or complex needs.

This role operates within a triage and prioritisation framework aligned with the ACT Shared Practice Framework and is delivered through multiple access points—phone, in-person, and outreach. Intake Case Workers collaborate closely with local service providers, including Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisations (ACCOs), to ensure culturally safe and effective responses.

The Salvation Army is committed to achieving a diverse workforce and strongly encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

How you will make an impact

  • Conduct holistic assessments using the ACT Shared Practice Framework.
  • Provide brief, goal-oriented interventions such as safety planning, crisis support, and short-term case coordination.
  • Refer clients to appropriate long-term supports and maintain active follow-up where required.
  • Record assessments and client data accurately in systems such as SAMIS or SHIP.
  • Deliver intake services via phone, in-office, and outreach locations.
  • Ensure cultural safety and accessibility across all service delivery modes.
  • Confirm client identity, consent, and risk factors through TSA protocols and sector systems.
  • Maintain current knowledge of local referral pathways and eligibility criteria.
  • Work collaboratively with ACCOs, government agencies, and other community services.
  • Participate in inter-agency meetings and shared referral processes.
  • Facilitate warm handovers to ensure continuity of care.
  • Engage in supervision, reflective practice, and case reviews.
  • Stay informed of legislative changes and best practice approaches.
  • Contribute to service improvement initiatives and co-design activities.
  • Actively participate in team planning, professional development, and service reviews.
  • Foster a positive, inclusive, and respectful team environment.
  • Uphold TSA values of compassion, integrity, respect, diversity, and collaboration.

What you will bring

  • Minimum Diploma in Community Services, Social Work, or a related field OR significant experience delivering case work or community support.
  • At least 1 year of case management experience, or substantial experience supporting vulnerable individuals and families.
  • Deep understanding of trauma-informed practice and the impact of poverty and systemic disadvantage.
  • Proven ability to deliver culturally safe services, including working with interpreters and liaison workers.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clear case notes and reports.
  • Knowledge of confidentiality, consent, privacy, and safeguarding responsibilities.
  • Excellent time management and the ability to prioritise effectively in a team setting.
  • Ability to respond appropriately to complex and unpredictable situations.
  • Proficiency in a language other than English.
  • Knowledge of the ACT service system, particularly in homelessness and financial wellbeing sectors.
  • Familiarity with SAMIS, SHIP, or similar case management/data reporting systems.

What We Offer

  • Salary packaging up to $15,900 tax free + $2,650 meal entertainment benefit.
  • Generous Paid Parental leave for primary (12 weeks) & secondary carers, Purchased Leave Scheme (up to 8 weeks) and 5 days paid leave per year to experience working in other TSA programs or activities.
  • Sorry Business and Ceremonial leave (up to 10 days)
  • Becoming part of our Burra Burra Network – a pastoral care network where regular group and topic-specific yarning circles are hosted to bring an awareness of the support and opportunities available
  • Access to EAP and health & wellness initiatives incl Fitness Passport
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities that enhance on the job skills and proficiency.
  • Rewarding and fulfilling purpose driven careers that have positive and sustainable / social impacts.

How to Apply

If you are ready to lead with purpose and help make a lasting difference in the ACT community, we want to hear from you.

Apply now with your resume and a cover letter addressing the key selection criteria.

The Salvation Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer who provides an inclusive work environment and embraces the diverse talent of its people. We value people of all cultures, languages, capacities, sexual orientations, gender identities and/or expressions. We are committed to achieving a diverse workforce and strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal people and Torres Strait Islander people.

The Salvation Army is a child safe organisation and is committed to protecting children and young people from harm. All child facing roles will require the successful completion of a Working with Children Check. Applicants for all roles require a mandatory Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check.

We value Integrity, Compassion, Respect, Diversity, and Collaboration

title: Venture and Founder Development Lead
description:
Te Whiwhinga mahi | The opportunity

This is a unique leadership opportunity to shape the University’s founder and venture development pathway and build the team that will deliver it.

Working at the intersection of innovation, entrepreneurship and commercialisation, you’ll lead a busy year-round portfolio that helps students, researchers and staff explore opportunities, validate ideas, develop as founders and progress early-stage ventures towards appropriate next-stage support.

You will:

  • Lead the strategic development, delivery and continuous improvement of CIE’s founder and venture development portfolio.

  • Shape a coherent pathway from early idea and exploration through validation, venture development and connection to appropriate next-stage support.

  • Build and lead a new Venture & Founder Development team, creating clear priorities, strong ways of working and consistently high-quality delivery.

  • Lead a diverse portfolio of founder and venture initiatives, ensuring programmes, cohorts, mentors, practitioners and external dependencies are well planned and coordinated.

  • Build trusted relationships with founders, researchers, academics, mentors, investors, industry, commercialisation colleagues and ecosystem partners.

  • Strengthen connections between CIE’s venture initiatives and wider opportunities for research translation, commercialisation, investment and venture support.

  • Use evidence, founder insights and emerging venture practices to inform portfolio decisions and continuously improve quality and founder outcomes.

  • Contribute as a member of CIE’s Leadership Team to the Centre’s strategy, performance, culture and organisational development.

This is a full-time (37.5 hours per week), permanent role. This is a salary band I role, with a salary range from $114,400 pa to $140,000 depending on skills and experience.

The nature of CIE’s programmes and events means the role requires flexibility to work outside normal business hours, including evening work as required and occasional weekend work.

For more detailed information, please refer to the Position Description.

Mō tō mātou rōpū | About the team

The Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (CIE) is Waipapa Taumata Rau’s platform for developing the innovators, entrepreneurs and changemakers of the future. We work across the University to help students, researchers and staff build innovation and entrepreneurial capability, turn ideas into action, develop ventures, and create social, cultural, environmental and economic impact for Aotearoa and the world.

CIE is entering an exciting new chapter. With an ambitious new strategy, we are significantly increasing the reach and impact of innovation and entrepreneurship across the University, helping realise Waipapa Taumata Rau’s ambition to be a global powerhouse of innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship, and strengthening the University’s contribution to a more innovative and prosperous Aotearoa.

We are building a team of people who are curious, collaborative, ambitious for impact and committed to turning ambition into action. If you want to help shape how a world-class research-led university develops innovative and entrepreneurial people, we would love to hear from you.

He kōrero mōu | About you

You are an experienced people and portfolio leader who combines strong venture and founder-development expertise with exceptional organisation, forward planning and execution. You understand what founders and early-stage ventures need as they move from an initial idea through exploration, validation and venture development, and you know how to turn that understanding into high-quality programmes and pathways.

You thrive in a fast-paced and varied environment and can lead a complex portfolio while building a new team and establishing the clarity, priorities and ways of working that enable people to perform at their best. You think ahead, anticipate dependencies and pressure points, and remain close enough to delivery to understand what is working, where quality can be strengthened and when intervention is needed.

You bring strong commercial judgement and can work credibly across different venture contexts, including student-led and research-derived ventures. You understand research translation and commercialisation and can work effectively with founders, researchers, academics, commercialisation professionals, investors, industry and the wider entrepreneurial ecosystem.

You are also a collaborative organisational leader. As a member of CIE’s Leadership Team, you will bring your expertise and perspective to collective decisions, work effectively across portfolio boundaries and take shared responsibility for CIE’s strategy, performance, culture and overall success.

You will bring:

  • Significant experience in venture and founder development, entrepreneurship, innovation, commercialisation or a related field.

  • Demonstrated success leading and developing people and building high-performing, collaborative teams.

  • Exceptional forward planning and portfolio-management capability, with experience leading multiple programmes or initiatives in complex, fast-moving environments.

  • Strong understanding of founder journeys and early-stage venture development, including opportunity exploration, validation and progression towards appropriate next-stage support.

  • Strong commercial judgement and an understanding of research translation and commercialisation.

  • Outstanding stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, with the credibility to work effectively with founders, researchers, academics, commercialisation professionals, investors, industry and ecosystem partners.

  • Experience coaching, mentoring or supporting founders as they navigate uncertainty, test assumptions and develop opportunities.

  • Strategic judgement and the ability to translate organisational priorities into coherent pathways, high-quality delivery and measurable outcomes.

  • Experience managing budgets, resources and operational planning.

  • A relevant tertiary qualification in business, innovation, entrepreneurship, science, engineering or a related discipline.

Experience in a tertiary education, research, innovation or entrepreneurship environment would be advantageous. An understanding of a research-led university environment, including the different contexts and motivations of students, researchers and academic staff, would be particularly valuable.

What we offer | Ngā āhuatanga kei a mātou

The University of Auckland is New Zealand’s leading university and maintains significant computational, laboratory and analytic facilities.

The University is committed to providing an excellent working environment through:

  • Flexible employment practices (including working from home, flexible hours)

  • Up to 6.75% company superannuation scheme

  • A competitive salary ($114,400 pa to $140,000 pa ) reflecting experience with five weeks’ annual leave

In addition, we also offer career development programmes, discounted car parking, a generous parental leave allowance, childcare, and a number of other discounts on internal and external services.

For more information, please visit Staff Benefits

Applications must be submitted online, by the closing date of Sunday 6th September, 2026 to be considered. title: Summer Internship: Backend/Frontend Software
description:
Are you interested in working on software with real-world impacts? At Monil, we write servers and client applications which improves the lives of both farmers and animals. We solve hard problems and work with large amounts of data, all with the goal of improving animal well-fare and farmers' productivity.

As a summer intern in Monil, you'll get to work on interesting problems where you'll have to use your own imagination and creativity in order to find good solutions to technical challenges. You'll work in collaboration with our experienced team of engineers, as well as with other departments, creating impactful solutions to actual problems.


The software team

Monil's software team creates and operates the infrastructure, backend servers and client applications used by our employees and users to interact with and monitor our smart collars. Our apps are implemented in React and Typescript, while the majority of our backend is written in Go. We store large amounts of data and statistics in our PostgreSQL and Timescale databases. We're not afraid to make big investments in order to provide the best tools possible for our users.

About the job

  • Join Monil's software team, developing software to interact with our smart animal collars

  • Help create the best possible, mission-critical tools for our users to interact with their livestock and our physical products, building fantastic visualizations based on large amounts of data.

  • Contribute to our frontend or backend apps, or a combination of the two.

The internship will begin in June, with the exact start date to be agreed upon. It will last for 6-8 weeks. The application deadline is October 6th.

It's beneficial if you have

  • 3+ years of relevant education or experience

  • Experience in one or more of the languages we use, such as Go, Typescript or Python

We can offer

  • An opportunity to make a real difference in Monil's products and services, innovating and applying creativity to solve real-world problems with high stakes.

  • A chance to spend a summer in a promising and well-backed scale-up with big ambitions in an early phase.

  • Work together with industry specialists in a variety of fields – from mechanics and electronics to embedded, backend and frontend software.

  • Competitive salary and benefits.

The Health and Safety Business Partner ensures that we provide a safe and healthy workplace and sustainable performance through the consistent delivery of health, safety and wellbeing practices in our homes.

Through effective stakeholder engagement, building capability and empowering local leadership, specialist advice, and coaching, this role is a true partner for our frontline leaders.

This role is based in Central Adelaide, South Australia.

Responsibilities:

Apply specialist knowledge and technical expertise to:

  • Provide quality proactive advice and support to Operational leaders and employees on a range of HSW issues.

  • Analyse and report on workplace incidents, hazards and injuries as well as trends in their area of responsibility.

  • Provide strategic advice and direction on complex claims and safety matters.

  • Ensure all incidents are investigated promptly & effectively and ensure appropriate corrective actions are identified and implemented.

  • Ensure notifiable incidents are reported to the state Regulator and internally as required.

  • Support the Injury management specialist with early intervention of injuries.

  • Collaborate with the National Health and Safety Manager and HSW team to develop and implement evidence-based risk reduction and improvement programs.

  • Foster a safety culture through role modelling safe workplace practices, such as consultation and identification of workplace hazards and risks.


The ideal person will have:

  • Experience in an WHS and Injury Management/Rehabilitation role South Australia, with a proven track record in delivering effective HSW performance results.

  • A customer service approach, strong analytical and problem solving skills and will be proactive.

  • Outstanding communication skills (both written and verbal).

  • Demonstrated ability to engage with external and internal stakeholders.

  • High level planning, time management and prioritising skills.

  • Demonstrated capability in interpreting and applying relevant WHS and workers compensation legislation.

The role is hybrid with regular travel, around three days per week, to our Central Adelaide, SA Homes. Some regional travel may be required.

As one of the largest and fastest growing aged care providers in Australia, we need exceptional people to join us on our journey of providing high quality person centred aged care and services. If this is you, Apply Now!

title: Palomies (3), Vaasa, Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue
location: Kaskinen, Korsnäs, Kristinestad, Kronoby, Laihia, Larsmo, Malax, Korsholm, Närpes, Pedersöre, Jakobstad, Nykarleby, Vaasa, Vöyri, Finland
description:
Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen tavoitteena ovat Suomen parhaat työntekijät. Haluamme panostaa henkilöstömme hyvinvointiin, henkilöstön riittävyyteen, hyvään johtamiseen ja sujuviin prosesseihin. Arvoihimme kuuluu toimia ihmiseltä ihmiselle. Hyvinvointialueellamme työskentelee yli 8000 eri alojen ammattilaista, jotka tarjoavat Pohjanmaan asukkaille laadukkaita ja turvallisia sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon sekä pelastustoimen palveluita.

Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen pelastuslaitos tarjoaa hyvähenkisen ja eteenpäin katsovan työyhteisön. Olemme aktiivisesti mukana pelastusalan valtakunnallisessa yhteistyössä. Työnantajana mahdollistamme täydennyskouluttautumisen sekä tuemme henkilökohtaisen osaamisen kehittämistä. Kannustamme kehittämään pelastuslaitosta oman osaamisesi sekä mielenkiintosi mukaan.

Haemme kolmea (3) palomiestä Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen pelastuslaitokselle. Palomiehen monipuoliseen tehtävänkenttään kuuluu mm. pelastustoiminta, sammuttaminen, ensihoito, vahingontorjunta ja omaisuuden suojaaminen ym. palomiehen tehtävät sekä muut esihenkilön määräämät tehtävät. Tehtäviin sisältyy myös kouluttamista ja harjoitusten pitoa. Palomies osallistuu onnettomuuksien ennaltaehkäisevään työhön niin valvonnan kuin valistuksen keinoin. Tehtäviä tehdään erilaisissa toimintaympäristöissä ja olosuhteissa. Työ on niin ryhmä-, pari- kuin yksintyöskentelyä.

Viran tuloksellisessa hoitamisessa apuna on hyvät työyhteisötaidot, oma-aloitteellisuus, suunnitelmallisuus, kehittämishalukkuus ja myönteinen asenne työtehtäviä kohtaan. Tarvitset myös tietoteknisiä valmiuksia.

Eduksi katsotaan vesisukelluskurssi (vesipelastussukeltajan pätevyys), pelastusalan täydennyskoulutukset ja muut toimintaa tukevat pätevyydet (esim. nostolavan käytön ja venepäällikön pätevyys).

Palomiehen viran palkkaus ja työaika määräytyvät henkilöstön virka- ja työehtosopimuksen mukaisesti (HYVTES) ja eläke-edut julkisten alojen eläkelain mukaisesti. Työaika on yleistyöaika 38,25 h/viikko ja/tai poikkeusluvan mukainen työaika, tällä hetkellä 40 h/vko. Tehtävään liittyy tarvittaessa varallaolo.

Virassa voidaan soveltaa kuuden (6) kuukauden koeaikaa. Valitun henkilön tulee tarvittaessa toimittaa hyväksyttävä selvitys terveydentilastaan ennen virkavalinnan vahvistamista. Lisäksi valittavan suostumuksella tehdään suppea henkilöturvallisuusselvitys turvallisuusselvityslain (726/2014) mukaan ja tähän liittyen esteetön vastaus on palvelussuhteen edellytyksenä.

Sijoituspaikkana pelastuslaitoksen alue, alkusijoituspaikka on Vaasa.


Kelpoisuusvaatimus:
Valtioneuvoston asetus pelastustoimesta 407/2011 6§, kohta 1.
Kyky ymmärtää ja käyttää maamme molempia kansalliskieliä.

Muut kelpoisuusvaatimukset:
Savusukelluskelpoisuus ja toimintakyky vaativiin tehtäviin, Firefit taso 3.0
Vähintään BC-luokan ajokortti.

title: Full Stack Engineer - Hybrid
description:
Link to process walkthrough: https://www.loom.com/share/3bc7e1ea87e2496aa7eee471d294b238

👋 Thanks for stopping by and learning more about this role at Sitemate! ✨🏗️

We'd love to hear from you 😊 👩‍💻👩🏽‍💻🧑🏿‍💻👨🏻‍💻

📝 Overview

Build What Matters

The Full Stack Engineer is an ownership role responsible for product outcomes end-to-end: from shaping technical approaches and building features through to release, reliability, and production performance.

At Sitemate, engineers combine strong technical craft with product thinking and delivery ownership. You'll work in small, high-trust teams alongside Product Design Managers to define problems, shape solutions, implement clean and scalable systems, and take responsibility for what ships — including how it behaves once live.

Engineering, product, and delivery are not separate handoffs here; they operate as one integrated team. We believe the future of product development in an AI-accelerated world belongs to engineers who can think beyond tickets - they own outcomes and deliver at speed with AI.

Employment:

  • Full-time

  • Based: Sydney, Australia or Melbourne, Australia

  • Remuneration (Including Super): AUD $85,000 - $200,000 pending your experience

About Sitemate

Sitemate builds modern software for construction, infrastructure, and industrial companies - helping teams move faster, work smarter, and deliver with confidence.

Our flagship platform, Dashpivot, transforms manual, paper-based processes into simple, mobile-first digital workflows. Teams use Sitemate every day to capture data in the field, automate reporting, and make better decisions in real time.

Since launching in 2018, we’ve grown from 5 to 150+ people across 18+ countries. We’re backed by Blackbird, Australia and New Zealand’s #1 venture capital firm, and graduated from the Startmate Accelerator. Thousands of companies use Sitemate tools today - with thousands more discovering us each month through strong word-of-mouth and organic growth.

Why Join Sitemate

At Sitemate, you’ll join a global team that values transparency, high velocity, hustle, diversity, and innovation.

We’re open about our metrics, honest about challenges, and obsessed with improving how the world’s most important industries operate. Our environment is flexible, fast-moving, and outcome-driven - designed to help you do the best work of your career.

You’ll be surrounded by people who take pride in their work, care deeply about results, and believe that great culture is built on trust, respect, and continuous learning.

How We Work

  • Transparency at every level: Monthly Allhands meetings share key company metrics, updates, and customer stories. We also spotlight a team member’s “Life Story” each month - it’s one of the ways we stay connected as a global team.

  • High velocity, low friction: Our systems are modern and fully integrated, so you’ll spend your time solving problems - not fighting tools.

  • Performance-driven growth: Seven of our last ten pay increases were made proactively, based on impact and results.

  • True flexibility: We focus on outcomes, not hours. You’ll have autonomy to manage your time and work where you perform best - with no time monitoring or unnecessary meetings.

  • Collaboration: You’ll work closely with other teams - engineering, product, design, marketing, and customer success - to move fast and deliver meaningful results.

  • Sydney HQ perks - rooftop garden, wellness centre, showers, and cycle storage in Haymarket

  • Melbourne office perks - micro-roasted coffee bar, on-site parking & bike storage, wellness & mothers rooms, opposite Southern Cross station

What We Offer

  • Competitive, performance-based remuneration

  • Equity options - own a piece of what you’re helping to build

  • 20 days of paid annual leave, plus sick, carer’s, and compassionate leave

  • Paid parental leave - 16 weeks for primary carers, 6 weeks for secondary carers (including adoption and stillbirth support)

  • Professional growth budget and a transparent career development framework

  • Laptop and home-office setup budget

  • Flexible work - remote or hybrid, plus the ability to work from anywhere for a few weeks each year

  • Community & connection - weekly team lunches, global offsites, and our signature “Life Story” sessions

Diversity & Inclusion

We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Sitemate welcomes people of all genders, ethnicities, ages, sexualities, and abilities.

55% of our team identify as coming from underrepresented ethnic backgrounds, 43% identify as female, and our team spans ages 22–51. We believe our diversity makes us stronger - and we’re committed to creating an environment where everyone can do their best work.

Learn More About Sitemate

🎧 Podcasts:

  • 2024: CEO Hartley Pike on scaling Sitemate, diversity, and culture

  • 2023: CMO Lance Hodgson on accelerating your career

  • 2022: CTO Tim Bray on building quality features that solve real customer problems

💬 Want to know what it’s like to work at Sitemate? Hear it straight from the team: People of Sitemate
⭐ Read what our customers say: G2 Crowd, Trust Radius
🎥 Team Offsites: 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025

What this role looks like at the mid level

You'll join a team attached to one of our products and have real ownership from early on, with the support of experienced engineers around you.

You'll work across frontend, backend, and mobile: TypeScript, React, Node.js, Angular, MongoDB, and AWS. You don't need to know all of these, willingness to learn matters more than what you know today.

🔧 Day-to-Day

  • Build and ship features with guidance from experienced teammates.

  • Work with AI tools daily, with the team's workflow skills for planning, implementation and review.

  • Fix bugs and improve product stability across web and mobile.

  • Investigate and resolve production issues.

  • Grow into more ownership over time, this role expands as you do.

⚡ Challenges

  • Our products seem simple to users but contain a high degree of technical complexity — shared components across multiple products, backend services powering web and mobile clients. There's a lot to learn.

  • Pace: we move quickly, so you'll need to be excited to learn fast.

  • We have a strong culture based on core values and operating principles. You may need to unlearn some habits from previous experience.

✅ Who This Role is For

  • You've built things you're proud of at a startup, in a side project, during a bootcamp, or at university.

  • You're deeply curious about AI-powered development and want to learn agentic engineering in a production environment.

  • You want to understand the customer problem, not just the code.

  • You're energised by learning fast in a supportive, high-tempo environment.

  • You want to be part of building something meaningful — our users build real infrastructure that shapes communities.

🚫 Who This Role is Not For

  • You prefer a slow ramp with months of onboarding before touching production code — here you'll ship early, with support.

  • You're not interested in owning the end-to-end delivery of features.

  • You're not interested in AI-first engineering practices, this is core to how we work, not optional.

🎯 Skills & Tools

Must Have:

  • Solid hands-on experience building and shipping production software

  • Hands on experience with AI-powered developer tools and agentic engineering practices.

  • Product mindset — wants to understand customer problems, not just implement tickets

  • Ability to work independently and take ownership of features end-to-end

Nice to Have:

  • TypeScript, React, Node.js, Angular, MongoDB, or AWS experience

  • Mobile development experience

  • Experience working in a fast-paced startup or product environment

Essential Tools:

  • TypeScript / JavaScript

  • React or Angular

  • Node.js

Bonus Tools:

  • MongoDB

  • AWS

  • React Native / mobile

PLEASE Note:

  • We do not use recruitment partners or services, so please save your time and don't reach out

title: Instruction Librarian (Temporary, Non-Sponored)
description:
Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q) is dedicated to fulfilling Georgetown University’s mission of promoting intellectual, ethical and spiritual understanding through serious and sustained discourse among people of different faiths, cultures, and beliefs. Embodying this spirit of the University, Georgetown’s Qatar campus undertakes education, research, and service in order to advance knowledge and provide students and the community with a holistic educational experience that produces global citizens committed to the service of humankind. We demonstrate the values of Georgetown University; seek to build upon the world-class reputation of the Edmund A. Walsh School of Foreign Service; and work with our partner, Qatar Foundation, in its endeavors to achieve the Qatar National Vision 2030.

Requirements

The Temporary Instruction Librarian serves as a primary liaison and instructional partner across assigned academic departments, designing and delivering responsive research and information literacy services that align with departmental curricula. This role will cultivate specialized library collections, advance scholarly communication, and develop collaborative outreach programs to enrich the academic and cultural life of the GU-Q community.

As this position is based in Doha, Qatar and offers no relocation assistance, GU-Q is looking for locally based candidates only. This is temporary, non-sponsored position that requires all applicants to already have the necessary sponsorship to live and work in Qatar.


Key Accountabilities:

  • Lead research sessions across assigned academic programs, aligning library instruction with departmental curriculum needs and delivering responsive services for students, faculty, staff and community researchers.

  • Develop and promote innovative services that support and advance information literacy, scholarly communication and academic excellence across campus.

  • Serve as liaison librarian for assigned subject areas, collaborating with departments to cultivate, evaluate, and build library collections that support curricular and research needs.

  • Support cultural engagement activities by helping design, promote, and implement programs that enrich GU-Q's academic and community life.

Key Activities:

Research and Instruction Services (50%)

  • Design and deliver instruction sessions, workshops, and course-integrated teaching on information literacy, AI literacy, database use, and research skills.

  • Provide advanced research consultations to faculty, students, and staff across multiple formats (in-person, online, and email).

  • Develop instructional materials and research guides using Springshare products and other content management platforms.

  • Support literature searching, research methodologies, citation management, and critical evaluation of information sources.

  • Help lead information & AI literacy initiatives to promote library resources and services.

  • Provide guidance on the ethical, effective, and discipline-appropriate use of AI in research and learning.

Liaison Services and Collection Development (20%)

  • Serve as a liaison to assigned academic departments (e.g., History, Economics, etc.), building strong partnerships with faculty, students, and staff.

  • Promote library services, tools, and resources within liaison areas through targeted outreach and engagement.

  • Evaluate, select, and recommend resources to support teaching and research in assigned liaison areas.

  • Monitor emerging publications and resources from leading publishers and vendors.

  • Regularly gather input from faculty on resource needs and priorities.

  • Assess usage, relevance, and gaps in collections, and collaborate with the acquisitions team on purchasing and renewal decisions.

Cultural and Community Engagement (20%)

  • Contribute to the planning and delivery of cultural, scholarly, and community engagement programs, such as speaker series, exhibitions, and thematic events.

  • Support outreach initiatives that enhance the visibility and impact of library services and programs.


Professional Development and Service (10%)

  • Engage in ongoing professional development to stay current with trends in librarianship, information literacy, AI, and emerging technologies, and subject areas.

  • Contribute to library committees, institutional service, and professional organizations.

  • Participate in cross-departmental initiatives and collaborative projects that advance the Library's strategic priorities.


Knowledge and Skills:

  • Demonstrated understanding of academic research processes, information literacy frameworks, instructional design, and scholarly communication (including open access, research impact, data literacy, and citation management).

  • Knowledge of AI and emerging technologies in higher education, including AI-assisted research tools, prompt design fundamentals, and responsible/ethical AI use.

  • Familiarity with research and instructional technologies, including citation management tools (e.g., Zotero, EndNote), bibliometric databases (e.g., Scopus, Web of Science), learning management systems (e.g., Canvas), and online tutorial platforms (e.g., LibGuides).

  • Familiarity with collection development, subject liaison services, reference models (virtual and in-person), and relevant library systems and research databases.

  • Ability to design and deliver effective instruction sessions, workshops, and learning materials, with strong classroom facilitation and public-speaking skills.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

  • Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships with faculty, students, and staff in an international academic environment.

  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and initiatives.

Qualifications:

  • Master's degree from an ALA-accredited program (or international equivalent) in Library and Information Science.

Experience:

  • 2+ years of professional experience in an academic library.

  • Experience with assessment and evaluation of library instruction and services, using qualitative and quantitative approaches.

    Current Georgetown Employees:

    If you currently work at Georgetown University, please exit this website and login to GMS () using your Net ID and password. Then select the Career worklet on your GMS Home dashboard to view Jobs at Georgetown.

    Submission Guidelines:

    Please note that in order to be considered an applicant for any position at Georgetown University in Qatar, you must submit a resume/CV for each position of interest. Documents are not kept on file for future positions.

    Need Assistance:

    Need some assistance with the application process? Contact us at guqhr@georgetown.edu.

    EEO Statement:

    GU is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, citizenship, color, disability, family responsibilities, gender identity and expression, genetic information, marital status, matriculation, national origin, race, religion, personal appearance, political affiliation, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

    Benefits:

    Georgetown University offers a wide variety of comprehensive and competitive benefits. Benefits packages include comprehensive health, dental and vision plans, disability and life insurance coverage, retirement savings programs, tuition assistance, voluntary insurance options (including group legal, accident, and critical illness), and much more. Whatever your need, the Office of Faculty and Staff Benefits will be standing by to support you. You can learn more about the benefits offered to eligible faculty and staff at or view the online interactive benefits guide for more information.
